payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #543, second landing: #423's follow-ups. #423 put each crate's integration tests in one binary (`--test it FILE::`), and a stale `--test it <module>::` filter then runs 0 tests and passes, where the old `--test <file>` failed loudly. This story makes the `--test it` filter gate exact and adds the runtime guard the issue's third ask names.

The branch story-543-filter-gate ends at e0c2666e, one commit over 58a77945 (a clean merge of main 12d0a867), over these commits off acc5df2a (#423's merge):
- 73e4060a, 9b429e9a: the gate finds a module's tests by parsing its source and holds a filter to a module that carries them (A3, A5), and judges a cfg_attr and a module's own #![cfg].
- 0477b859: the gate rebuilt on the binaries' own `--list` (operator ruling, 2026-10-05: the list is the fact, not the source text).
- c9777419: a filter is held to the binary of the command's own build configuration.
- ce7b292c: on the operator's ruling of 2026-10-06 (BOTH, recorded on #543). (1) Every flag that can move the build refuses, as do more than one -p, CARGO_*/RUST* assignments and a non-dev profile for brokkr-cli's own list. (2) The runtime guard scripts/run-it-tests.sh: a filtered `it` run that executes 0 tests fails. Every `--test it` line in .github/ and scripts/ goes through it, and the gate refuses one that does not.
- 58318f9b, e2d074f2: the guard decides on every `test result:` summary the run prints, the unterminated last line included, by number. Ignored and filtered-out counts are not execution, and a run with no summary or an unreadable one refuses. The last round (implement-story-543-423-follow-u-49cadeb8) ruled residual at LOW, and the coverage gate and host lints were green.
- (controller, after the first landing) a one-line portability fix: the unreadable-list row runs /usr/bin/false, because macOS has no /bin/false and PR #573's test (macos-latest) failed on it. The first landing (landing-pr-for-story-543-423-s-f-2f2d1375) ruled residual at LOW with no security residual on 58a77945; this commit is the only change since.
Commits 9b429e9a and 0477b859 were written by GLM and the rest by DeepSeek Flash or Claude. The controller re-signed the chain with identical trees, because main requires verified signatures.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge:
1. That no `--test it` command in the guarded roots (.github/, scripts/) can run 0 tests and pass. Either the line gate refuses it (unknown module or name, a build-moving word, several packages) or the guard fails the run (zero selected, ignored-only, no summary, an unread summary, any summary that executed nothing). The ten real lines still run, each with its test count unchanged.
2. That every refusal is exact and bound: each row asserts status and text, and each has a compiling removal control in a commit message. No refusal weakened across the six rounds.
3. That the guard passes a failing command's own status and output through, and that its header says exactly when its own exit replaces the command's.
4. That the merge with main changes neither side's behaviour, and that #423's layout holds (layering::test_targets passes on the merged tree).
5. That the carried LOWs are listed for the PR, each for the operator: the bash width arithmetic (fail-closed), H3, H4, A4, L3 (measure-budgets.sh's appended flags and `|| true`), L4(a), and the commands outside the guarded roots (quality/measure.sh:105 and a recipe's role scripts; whether they join the guarded roots is the operator's ruling), and the false-summary wrapper class the ruling accepted.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

For the implement phase only: if a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run, all clean:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy on the crates you touched, with -D warnings
- typos --hidden
- shellcheck -S warning on each .sh you change
- quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api

Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json

  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
```

members.adversarial:
Adversarial read-only review of e0c2666e over prior landing 58a77945, with the story and main merge checked against 12d0a867. Verdict residual at LOW; no new finding, no unresolved high/critical finding and no security residual under the operator's stated threat model. No tracked file changed and no commit made.

The sole new diff replaces /bin/false with /usr/bin/false in the unreadable-list row and its exact expected error. It continues to exercise a successfully launched process exiting 1, rather than an absent executable on macOS. The original compiling removal control is recorded in 0477b859: disabling listed's exit-status check changes this assertion to Ok({}). No production gate/guard or refusal changed. The merge's only file differing from both parents is tests/it.rs, combining main's capability_artifacts module with the branch's run_it_tests module; the merged #423 layout assertion passes. Frozen contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference have no story diff.

Validation performed here: layering::test_targets 18/18 and run_it_tests 5/5 pass; fmt and git diff --check pass; bundles/self compiles. The ten tracked --test it lines are held by the real-list gate. The three guarded-root commands were run directly: packaging 23 passed, ignored exact suppression 1 passed (BROKKR_SUPPRESSION_BASE=12d0a867), budgets 4 passed. Binary lists retain research_registry 2, witness_digests 6, suppressions 7 and each exact suppression name 1; blessing/regeneration commands were not executed because this seat is read-only.

Independent in-memory guard probes: zero counts, ignored-only, no summary, unread summary, positive then zero, zero then positive, and unterminated zero/unread after positive all exit 1, preserving captured output bytes. A positive summary exits 0; an executed failing test's summary preserves exit 101 and bytes. In-memory removal controls for plain read, exit 0 instead of command status, and string comparison of counts each wrongly exit 0 where the actual guard refuses/preserves failure. Source, exact variant/text assertions, and recorded controls in 0477b859, c9777419, ce7b292c, 58318f9b and e2d074f2 were examined; no refusal weakened. The header accurately names summary refusals that replace the command's status. Output buffering and merging stderr into stdout remain the previously recorded limitation.

Carried LOWs for the operator and PR, unchanged by this landing:
1. Bash count arithmetic (0071 rulings 3/9): 18446744073709551616 passed wraps to zero and falsely refuses, fail-closed; 08 passed produces an octal diagnostic and accepts the positive summary. Both reproduced. Actual libtest counts never have these spellings; all-zero counts refuse. This belongs to the accepted false-summary producer class.
2. H3 (ruling 8): hand-written Refusal Display and Result<_, String> in test helpers. The recorded reason is no thiserror dependency in brokkr-cli's test target; the operator ruled no change.
3. H4 (ruling 9): crates/ is outside the scanned roots, so Rust command literals, including deliberate stale fixtures, are not held.
4. A4 (ruling 3): a YAML double-quoted run scalar spelling --test with unicode/hex escapes is not recognized from raw bytes, so an unguarded stale command can evade the text gate. This remains the previously accepted exotic-spelling LOW under the 2026-09-26 threat model, not a newly opened refusal.
5. L3 (rulings 5/9): measure-budgets.sh report appends libtest flags beyond the scanned line and swallows status with || true; a stale budgets filter fails later on missing measurement data. Commands assembled from text without spelling --test it are likewise outside the grammar.
6. L4(a) (ruling 9): a stale suffix such as packaging::no_such_test passes the module-only text hold; the runtime guard refuses it in guarded roots. --skip/ignored-only selections are also protected there by the summary guard.
7. Commands outside guarded roots (ruling 9): quality/measure.sh:105 and recipes/research/roles/verify-seat.sh:47 remain held only by the text gate. Whether quality/ and recipe role scripts join the guarded roots is the operator's ruling.
8. Accepted false-summary wrapper class (rulings 3/9): a producer executing no test but printing a well-formed positive test result summary passes an output-based guard.
The prior LOW evidence limitation also remains: some looped configuration/assignment controls record only their first failing row; the rows bind, but not every row's observed failure is separately recorded.

This seat did not rerun the full workspace suite, clippy or host ratchets; the run's verify result is pass. Exact coverage is the controller's and was not run. macOS execution, final-head remote CI, publication and signature verification are not claimed by this seat.
members.correctness:
Read-only correctness/fit review at e0c2666e: inspected git history, the sole 58a77945..HEAD delta, the story diff against main 12d0a867, README, decisions 0004/0005/0051/0071, gate/guard/tests and recorded removal controls. No fixes or commits. The sole new change uses /usr/bin/false on Linux and macOS and retains the exact failed-list status/text assertion; no new finding above LOW. Observed: layering::test_targets plus run_it_tests, 23 passed; guarded packaging 23, explicitly executed ignored suppression 1, budgets 4, each exit 0; fmt and diff checks clean; bundles/self compiles. The real-tree gate holds the existing commands and #423 layout passes. Every summary, including an unterminated last line, is checked; zero executed, ignored-only, absent and unreadable summaries refuse, and accepted failing runs preserve status/output, with the header correctly explaining replacement. Merge 58a77945 differs from both parents only in tests/it.rs, main's modules plus mod run_it_tests; gate/guard unchanged. Story diff modifies no frozen contract, fixture, production policy or reference bytes. All ten existing command lines retain their argv except the intended guard prefix; the only subsequent change touches the portability row.

Carried findings for the operator/PR, all LOW, decision 0071: F1 ruling 9, scripts/run-it-tests.sh:43 uses bounded Bash arithmetic: overflow can falsely refuse a positive count (fail-closed); synthetic invalid-octal/positive summaries belong to F8's accepted wrapper class, so that broader class is not exclusively fail-closed. F2 H3, ruling 8: Refusal has manual Display and built_it/listed and lexer helpers return Result<_, String>; retained reason: test code lacks thiserror, strings are explanatory UnreadList.why, operator ruled no change. F3 H4, ruling 9: crates/ is outside RUN_COMMANDS, leaving embedded Rust commands unheld; retained reason: needs a Rust literal/comment reader and scope ruling, deliberately stale gate fixtures must be distinguished. F4 A4, rulings 3/9: YAML escaped flag spellings that never textually name --test evade the raw trigger and Unguarded requirement; accepted exotic spelling under accidental-misuse scope. F5 L3, ruling 9: program-generated argv such as xargs is unseen; scripts/measure-budgets.sh:27 appends flags and absorbs guard status with || true, relying on required report records instead; knowingly retained measurement behavior. F6 L4(a), ruling 9: non-exact filters are checked only by their first module segment; stale suffixes pass the line gate, with the runtime guard closing ordinary guarded runs. F7 ruling 9: quality/measure.sh:105 and recipes/research/roles/verify-seat.sh:47 remain outside guarded roots, allowing zero selections to succeed; root expansion is the operator's ruling. F8 rulings 3/9: accepted false-summary/wrapper class, arbitrary producers can print a positive summary without executing tests and the grammar cannot prove an arbitrary wrapper invokes the guard; accepted threat-model limit. F9 ruling 9: per-row compiling removal-control evidence remains incomplete for older looped configuration/assignment/host cases; 58318f9b corrects records to first-row failures and e2d074f2 records later summary controls, not every older row independently. These assertions bind; this is evidence debt rather than a test that cannot fail.
